text:
Aisha Garcia: FYI we kick off BigCorp POC next week. Security wants a short note: compare VPC peering vs PrivateLink, exact SG/firewall rules, whether Redwood needs any inbound reachability into their VPC, and a short list of escalation contacts. Can ops/SEs help? cc @Marco Liu @Jordan Patel

Marco Liu: TL;DR: both supported. Pick VPC peering for max throughput and simpler network path if CIDRs don't overlap. Pick PrivateLink when CIDRs overlap or customer policy forbids peering. PrivateLink gives interface endpoints + private DNS.

Jordan Patel: Adding multi-cloud notes: GCP - use VPC peering or Private Service Connect (PSC). Azure - use Private Endpoint (Private Link) or VNet peering. For docs I'll include quick Terraform examples.

Priya Kapoor: Here's the minimal firewall/SG guidance I hand out (AWS examples):
- Outbound TLS to Redwood control plane and model API: TCP 443 -> redwood-control-egress.example.net or 52.21.34.0/24 (we provide live list)
- If using VPC Peering: allow TCP 443 and 50051 (gRPC) between customer CIDR <-> redwood-peered-cidr (e.g., 10.200.0.0/16)
- If using PrivateLink: allow outbound TCP 443 to the ENI IPs that AWS creates for the interface endpoints (these are in customer's subnets)
- For streaming/long-lived connections: ensure NAT egress IPs are stable (use EIP) or put an egress proxy behind a fixed IP
- No inbound firewall rules on customer VPC required for typical setups; customer initiates outbound connections.

Tom Reynolds: Security addendum: we use TLS for control plane. For Private deployments we support mTLS for control plane RPCs on 50051; for Hosted control-plane we require HTTPS (server cert validation). Provide our certificate fingerprint on request. Also include an allowlist URL for our public egress IP ranges (we rotate; link to live JSON).

Aisha Garcia: Can you paste a short example SG rule set we can put in the questionnaire? They asked for literal lines to copy/paste.

Priya Kapoor: Copy/paste friendly snippet: 
- CUSTOMER_SG outbound: 
  - Type: HTTPS 
  - Protocol: TCP 
  - Port: 443 
  - Destination: 52.21.34.0/24 (redwood control plane, refer to live list)
- CUSTOMER_SG outbound (peering): 
  - Protocol: TCP 
  - Ports: 443, 50051 
  - Destination: 10.200.0.0/16 (example peered Redwood VPC)
- CUSTOMER_SG outbound (PrivateLink): 
  - Protocol: TCP 
  - Port: 443 
  - Destination: <ENI_PRIVATE_CIDR_BLOCKS_CREATED_BY_AWS>
- If your environment requires explicit NAT EIPs: allow 443 from those EIPs.

Jordan Patel: Terraform snippet for AWS PrivateLink we give customers (replace service_name):
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "rw_private" {
  vpc_id            = var.vpc_id
  service_name      = "com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-xxxxxxx"
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  subnet_ids        = var.subnets
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.rw_ep_sg.id]
}

Jordan Patel: GCP Private Service Connect example (service attachment on our side + PSC consumer on theirs) will be in the doc as well.

Tom Reynolds: Also include operational requirements for the POC:
- Verify CIDR non-overlap or choose PrivateLink/PSC
- Provide stable egress IPs or allowlist our egress list
- Enable VPC Flow Logs / Firewall logs for the POC window (recommended)
- Share contact: infra-ops@redwood.ai and se-oncall@redwood.ai for urgent network issues

Aisha Garcia: BigCorp also asked whether we ever require inbound connections into their VPC (they worry about opening inbound).

Marco Liu: Short: No inbound rules are required for standard customer-initiated traffic. Exception: if the customer requests that we mount a specific service into their VPC (rare), that would require peering + specific inbound rules and a documented change request. We'll note that in the questionnaire.

Priya Kapoor: Edge cases to call out in the one-pager: 
- Overlapping CIDR => PrivateLink/PSC/Azure Private Endpoint recommended
- Large file uploads / heavy egress => peering preferred for throughput and predictable MTU
- Latency-sensitive streaming => peering reduces hops

Tom Reynolds: Security FAQ entries to include: 
- Q: Do you support IP allowlisting? A: Yes  provide NAT EIPs or use our live CIDR list -> https://redwood.ai/egress-ips.json
- Q: Do you inspect packet payloads? A: No for standard hosted customers; we only terminate TLS at our control plane. If customers require dedicated appliances we can discuss alternatives.

redwood-bot: Upload complete: docs/presales/1719901234-bigcorp-network-onepager.pdf -> s3://redwood-internal/docs-presales/1719901234-bigcorp-network-onepager.pdf

Aisha Garcia: Awesome. Jordan, Marco can you review the PDF and add anything missing? I'll attach to the security questionnaire once it's final. POC start Mon 2024-08-05.

Jordan Patel: Reviewing now. Will add GCP PSC note and a short diagram showing split-horizon DNS for PrivateLink.

Marco Liu: Looks good to me. No blockers.

Priya Kapoor: No blockers from security rules side.

Tom Reynolds: All set.

Aisha Garcia: Thanks team! :rocket:
